source.title: Mild/Moderate Asthma Network in Italy (MANI): a long-term observational study
source.source_type: prospective observational cohort study design/network description
source.source_file: Mild Moderate Asthma Network in Italy MANI a long-term observational study.pdf

extraction_metadata.scope_note: This article reports the design and planned methods of MANI. It does not report enrolled-cohort outcomes. Background claims attributed to cited literature and bibliography entries were not atomized as primary-study findings.

atoms.canonical_statement: MANI was designed to prospectively characterize the epidemiological evolution of mild and moderate asthma and to generate long-term real-world data on disease progression, management, and prognosis.
The planned MANI cohort comprises at least 20,000 male and female adults aged 18 to 80 years with mild-to-moderate asthma defined according to GINA 2020.

population.label: Adults aged 18-80 years with mild-to-moderate asthma defined according to GINA 2020

atoms.canonical_statement: MANI is described as a cluster-based, real-world, cross-sectional, prospective, observational cohort study.
The study was launched by the Italian Respiratory Society and the Italian Society of Allergology, Asthma and Clinical Immunology, which established an intersociety scientific committee.
A non-probability sample of consecutive patients referred to recruiting outpatient clinics is planned across 200 pulmonology and allergology centers distributed throughout Italy.
Inclusion requires adulthood, specialist-diagnosed asthma according to GINA, and a scheduled visit to a respiratory or allergy clinic.

population.label: Eligible MANI participants
inclusion_criteria: Adult diagnosed with asthma by a specialist according to GINA
Scheduled to visit a respiratory or allergy clinic

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with severe asthma according to the cited ERS/ATS severe-asthma definition are excluded.

population.label: Excluded from MANI
exclusion_criteria: Severe asthma according to the cited ERS/ATS definition

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with interstitial lung disease, pulmonary neoplasms, or current lung infections are excluded.
Patients with immunological disorders requiring immunosuppressants or continuous oral corticosteroid treatment are excluded.

population.label: Excluded from MANI
exclusion_criteria: Immunological disorder requiring immunosuppressants or continuous oral corticosteroids

atoms.canonical_statement: Participation in previous or concomitant observational studies does not preclude MANI enrollment.

population.label: Eligible MANI participants
inclusion_criteria: May participate in previous or concomitant observational studies

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants receive study information for themselves and their general practitioner and must provide written consent.
Enrollment was planned to start in May 2021 and continue until the target sample size is reached; follow-up is planned for 10 years starting from enrollment of the last patient.
Follow-up scheduling is based on the GINA document and each center's plan.
The study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04796844.
The primary outcome is the epidemiological evolution of mild and moderate asthma, operationalized as disease severity according to GINA during prospective observation.

atoms.canonical_statement: At enrollment, investigators collect patient history, asthma characteristics, comorbidities, available spirometry and imaging results, questionnaire responses, self-rated asthma control, and laboratory tests for allergy and airway inflammation.

Follow-up data on asthma control, lung function, and environmental exposure are collected using questionnaires at least every 6 to 12 months to assess outcomes and exacerbation-related aggravating factors.
The case report form is intended to mirror data routinely reported in medical records, and the treating physician transfers medical-record data to the analysis platform.
An ad hoc REDCap web case report form is used for MANI data collection.
Each participating center receives credentials for a reserved area of the web application, and the article states that the connection uses HTTPS and passwords are stored with MD5 coding.
Each registered patient is assigned a study identification code constructed from portions of the patient name and surname, date of birth, gender, and province of residence.
Centers can view and edit clinical data for their own patients but can view only general descriptive statistics for patients enrolled by other centers.

Qualitative variables are planned to be summarized as absolute and relative frequencies, while quantitative variables are planned to be summarized as mean with standard deviation or median with interquartile range according to distribution.
The incidence of different forms of asthma is planned to be reported with 95% confidence intervals.
Cox proportional hazards regression is planned to assess demographic, clinical, and epidemiological variables in relation to asthma evolution.
Statistical analyses are planned in STATA version 16.
The sample-size plan assumes that at least 20,000 participants are needed to detect an estimated 8% incidence for the primary outcome with beta error 0.1 and alpha error 0.05.

The protocol states that the study will follow Good Clinical Practice, the Helsinki and Oviedo declarations, and listed Italian legal requirements, with informed consent from eligible participants who agree to participate.
The authors state that MANI aims to identify mild/moderate asthma clusters using sociodemographic data, clinical data, and patient-reported outcomes.
The authors propose that study results may support cluster-specific analytic strategies focused on individual aggravating factors during exacerbations and on disease progression.
The authors acknowledge that the observational study design limits causal interpretation.
The authors acknowledge that recruitment in Italian secondary care limits generalizability to other settings.
The authors expect the large cohort to improve understanding of the epidemiological evolution of mild and moderate asthma and provide insights into clinical management.

The article argues that longitudinal real-world studies are needed to assess transferability of clinical research findings, long-term effectiveness of recommended strategies, and opportunities to alter disease evolution.
The authors report no conflicts of interest.
The study is described as nonprofit and supported by the Italian Respiratory Society and the Italian Society of Allergology, Asthma and Clinical Immunology.
The article states that datasets used or analyzed during the study will be available from the study steering committee upon reasonable request.
